name: Sara
personalityTraits: Labels problems as 'personality differences' rather than addressing them
Eventually needs to facilitate the final group discussion

communicationStyle.tone: Diplomatic and slightly evasive — defaults to softening language that avoids naming the real issue
tendencies: Reframes conflict as a matter of style rather than accountability
Uses group consensus as cover for not making a decision herself
Responds well to players who give her a concrete, face-saving path forward
Will act more decisively if the player names the pattern without attacking her

knownFacts: The group is divided over Evan
Evan's behaviour has caused conflict within the team
Gossip about Evan is spreading among group members
doesNotKnow: The original version of the rumour — she has only heard the mutated form
The difference between Evan's impact on Daniel and Evan's actual intention
How the group's exclusion of Evan has affected his behaviour and defensiveness
How her own avoidance of confrontation has allowed the label to grow unchecked

emotionalState.baseline: Anxious and conflict-averse — prioritises the appearance of harmony over resolving the underlying issue; genuinely wants a good outcome but lacks the courage to create one

worsensIf: Player forces a binary choice (keep Evan or remove him) without offering a middle path
Player calls out her avoidance directly in an accusatory way
Group tension escalates visibly in front of her without resolution
improvesIf: Player proposes a specific, actionable rule she can adopt as a leadership decision
Player frames the issue as a process problem rather than a people problem
Player acknowledges both Daniel's frustration and Evan's missing context before asking her to decide

storyRole: Represents passive leadership and conflict avoidance — her inaction gives the 'Alien' label room to solidify; the final meeting is her chance to either enable exclusion or model healthy boundary-setting
